newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly hold steady, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly hold steady, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly held steady Wednesday in lackluster trade, with sliding NYMEX energy prices taking some of the steam out of the recent fuel oil rally, industry sources said.

"Crude has been an important factor (in the resid price gains), but it better get cold quick or I don't see these numbers holding," said one cash trader, noting cheaper gas and relatively mild East Coast weather were cutting fuel burns.
In New York Harbor, one percent was unchanged at about $21.25 a barrel, with a prompt, one percent barge seller looking for $21.80, traders said.
NYH high sulphurs notionally eased slightly, with 2.2 percent now pegged at $19.25-50.
At the U.S. Gulf, high sulphur remained firmly in the mid-$20 area, while one percent notionally held at about the same level though some thought the grades were backwardated.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
New York City gate gas prices jumped about 15 cents Wednesday to about the $2.60/mmBtu level, still very competitive with NYH one percent resid at a $3.37/mmBtu equivalent.
